public_rationale: OpenAI's February 15, 2024 research-preview example shows Sora failing to model a chair as rigid, producing inaccurate physical interactions [e3]. This supports the clause that physical laws are not reliably enforced, but does not establish that the model never represents physical dynamics [e3]. The January 14, 2025 multi-model study reports limited physical understanding and some successful test cases, but does not settle physical modeling in the February 2024 Sora snapshot [e4]. The categorical claim that no physics is ever modeled remains unresolved [e3, e4].
limitations: The chair example demonstrates an output failure, not the absence of all learned physical representations.
The later multi-model study is not a decisive test of the February 2024 snapshot.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Sora never models actual physics, and the entities in its videos are not constrained by physical laws.

statement.excerpt: No actual physics is ever modeled, and the entities depicted are not constrained by the laws of physics.

from_speaker: No actual physics is ever modeled
the entities depicted are not constrained by the laws of physics
our_interpretation: The word ever makes the first clause a categorical claim about the absence of physical modeling, including learned physical representations.
The second clause is read as saying physical laws are not reliably enforced in generated scenes.
An absence of an explicitly programmed physics engine would not by itself establish an absence of learned physical modeling.
The target is the February 2024 research-preview snapshot, the latest publicly documented version before the post.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes both the absence of physical modeling in the contemporaneous model and the absence of reliable physical-law enforcement in its outputs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Controlled evidence establishes that the contemporaneous model represents and uses physical dynamics, or reliably enforces the relevant physical laws.
